questions.stem: Concerning extracellular matrix pathologies (one or more correct answers):
options: In scurvy, vascular anomalies are linked to anomalies in the synthesis of type III collagen
Fibrosis is characterized by an increase, in a tissue, of the constituents of the mitochondrial matrix
Some genetic diseases can affect collagen synthesis
Scurvy is due to a deficiency of vitamin C, which is a cofactor of collagen synthesis
questions.explanation: No official answer key for this exam — answers worked out from the course. Fibrosis is an increase of the extracellular matrix.

options: Archaea have rRNAs similar to those of eukaryotes
Archaea are very similar to bacteria morphologically and metabolically
Viruses have a cytoplasm and a true nucleus
Viruses are obligate parasites with no metabolism of their own
questions.explanation: No official key for this exam; answer aligned with the official 2024-2025 key for the same statements (archaeal rRNAs differ from those of eukaryotes).

questions.stem: Concerning the termination step of protein synthesis:
options: Initiation factors are involved
The tRNA–peptide ester bond is cleaved by peptidyltransferase, which acts as a hydrolase
The complete protein chain is released and the two ribosomal subunits release the mRNA without dissociating
Peptidyltransferase has no role in termination and only acts in forming peptide bonds
questions.explanation: No official key — release factors are involved and the subunits dissociate.

questions.stem: Concerning transport across the plasma membrane:
options: Receptor-induced pinocytosis is a specific, selective form of endocytosis not involving membrane receptors
Raft endocytosis leads to the formation of caveolae whose membrane is rich in protein domains
Facilitated transport works along the molecular gradient
Symports couple passive and active transport in opposite directions
questions.explanation: No official key — symports move both solutes in the same direction; caveolae are rich in cholesterol/sphingolipids (rafts).

questions.stem: The structure of bacteria always contains:
options: Pili
A capsule
An envelope containing viral proteins
A plasma membrane
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: About protein glycosylation in the rough endoplasmic reticulum:
options: The preformed oligosaccharide motif (2 N-acetylglucosamines, 9 mannoses and 3 glucoses) is transferred from dolichol-phosphate to an N-glycosylation consensus sequence containing asparagine
The oligosaccharide motifs are only modified after the glycoprotein is transferred to the Golgi apparatus
N-glycosylation takes place in the RER lumen during translation
O-glycosylation indicates the extent of protein folding so that proteins only leave the ER once correctly folded
questions.explanation: No official key — trimming starts in the ER; the folding quality control uses the N-glycan (calnexin cycle).

options: Is a proteoglycan
Is a glycosaminoglycan
Is necessarily associated with a protein core to form a proteoglycan
Attracts water, a property essential for resistance to compressive forces
questions.explanation: No official key — hyaluronic acid is a free GAG, not bound to a core protein.

options: Viruses of eukaryotes can be RNA or DNA viruses
They can be classified by the type of capsid symmetry, helical or cubic
They have no metabolism of their own nor intrinsic capacity to produce the proteins encoded by their genome
Coronaviruses are RNA viruses whose name comes from their shape, with spikes forming a kind of crown
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: The molecular mechanisms involved in contact inhibition can be studied on a line of:
options: Lymphocytes at confluence
Adherent cells at confluence
Adherent cancer cells at confluence
Adherent cells at semi-confluence
questions.explanation: No official key — cancer cells lose contact inhibition; lymphocytes are not adherent.

options: Among its frequent constituents are collagen IV, nidogen and keratins
Is part of the extracellular matrix
Is made of parallel collagen fibers forming a dense bundle
Is a fibrous network made of glycoproteins and proteoglycans
questions.explanation: No official key — keratins are intracellular intermediate filaments.

options: Can transduce signals from the extracellular matrix to the cell
Are transmembrane receptors
Consist of an α subunit and a β subunit
Bind to extracellular matrix molecules
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: Concerning the principles of cell theory:
options: Every living organism is composed of one or more cells
All living beings must be composed of simple elementary structures that do not repeat
Every cell comes from the division of another pre-existing cell
The cell is the unit of structure and function of life
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: Ribosomes bound to the ER membrane make membrane proteins destined:
options: For the outer face of the plasma membrane (external peripheral proteins)
For the membrane of the Golgi apparatus
For other cell membranes: peroxisomes, lysosomes and mitochondria
For the plasma membrane
questions.explanation: No official key — most peroxisomal and mitochondrial proteins are made on free ribosomes.

options: Desmin depolymerization starts from the microtubule organizing center
Tubulin is part of the zonula adherens
Dynein provides centripetal transport and kinesin centrifugal transport
In cell fractionation, the first pellet obtained after differential ultracentrifugation contributes to the study of cytoskeletal elements
questions.explanation: No official key — desmin is an intermediate filament; zonula adherens uses actin.

options: Detoxification is an important function of the SER
The active site of cytochrome P450 is on the cytosolic side of the SER
P450 action hydroxylates the drug, increasing its water solubility
In the SER lumen, the hydroxylated drug undergoes glucuronidation, which increases its solubility
questions.explanation: No official key.

options: Protein synthesis always starts at the RER
Translation ends when the ribosome reaches the stop codon of the mRNA
The elongation step involves elongation factors
Protein synthesis requires tRNAs that match a given amino acid to each anticodon of the mRNA
questions.explanation: No official key — synthesis starts on free ribosomes; mRNA carries codons, not anticodons.

questions.stem: The study of microtubule dynamics during cell division requires the use of:
options: Fluorochromes
Flow cytometry
Transmission electron microscopy
Confocal fluorescence microscopy
questions.explanation: No official key — dynamics require live imaging with fluorescence.

options: Are composed of hydrophilic lipids
Can change configuration while transporting molecules
Modify the molecule they transport
Always carry out transport down the chemical gradient
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: Which laboratory techniques keep cells alive?
options: Flow cytometry
Cell fractionation
Fluorescent immunolabeling
Immortalization by viral transfection
questions.explanation: No official key.

options: Are never linked to sugar chains, unlike proteins
All have a hydrophilic domain and a hydrophobic domain
Phosphatidylserine and phosphatidylethanolamine are found mainly in the inner leaflet
Can move slowly from one leaflet of the bilayer to the other
questions.explanation: No official key — glycolipids exist; flip-flop is slow.

questions.stem: The combination (Taxol + fluorescent immunolabeling) makes it possible to visualize:
options: The framework of microvilli
The microtubules of cell division
The intermediate filaments present in stem cells
The mitotic contractile ring
questions.explanation: No official key — Taxol stabilizes microtubules.

questions.stem: About the functions of the endoplasmic reticulum:
options: The RER synthesizes proteins destined for the constitutive and regulated secretory pathway
The SER is involved in sulfation
The RER is the site of some glycosylation processes
The SER is the site of biosynthesis of lipids destined for the cell membrane
questions.explanation: No official key — sulfation occurs in the Golgi.

options: G-actin-ATP is found only in the cytosol
Nucleation of F-actin occurs anywhere in the cytosol
The basic unit and the basic protein are the same
Depolymerization occurs at the microtubule organizing center
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: About protein folding in the RER:
options: After synthesis in the RER, misfolded proteins are sent by vesicles to lysosomes for degradation
Folding depends on chaperone proteins that help and control folding
When proteins misfold in the RER, the cell goes into apoptosis
Folding gives the three-dimensional conformation needed for their function
questions.explanation: No official key — misfolded proteins are retro-translocated to the proteasome (ERAD).

options: Microtubule tubulin undergoes N-glycosylation in the RER, essential for its polymerization
Intermediate filaments are not involved in cell division
They all have the same diameter
Some can take part in the intracellular movement of organelles
questions.explanation: No official key.

options: A tRNA with a specific codon can carry different amino acids
tRNAs are small double-stranded RNA molecules
An mRNA can be translated by several ribosomes at once, producing several identical proteins from the same messenger
tRNAs contain a three-nucleotide sequence, the anticodon, whose bases are complementary to the mRNA codon
questions.explanation: No official key.

options: The cell coat helps maintain plasma membrane asymmetry
The hydrophilic regions of transmembrane proteins are all exposed on the cytosolic side
Peripheral membrane proteins are amphipathic
The lipid composition of the two leaflets is different, reflecting the identical functions of the two faces
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: Events in the maturation of ribosomal RNAs and formation of eukaryotic ribosomes include:
options: Synthesis of a 45S pre-rRNA molecule
Incorporation of 18S rRNA into the large ribosomal subunits
Association of ribosomal proteins with rRNAs before these molecules leave the nucleus
Synthesis of a 5S rRNA molecule in the nucleolus
questions.explanation: No official key — 18S goes to the small subunit; 5S rRNA is transcribed outside the nucleolus.

options: Allows diffusion against the concentration gradient of the transported molecule
Is saturable
Is involved exclusively in the diffusion of lipid-soluble molecules
Requires energy from ATP hydrolysis
questions.explanation: No official key.

options: The macromolecules making up the extracellular matrix are produced locally by cells in the matrix
Elastin ensures adhesion of cells to the extracellular matrix
Hyaluronic acid is a glycosaminoglycan that exists in the free state in the extracellular matrix
All glycosaminoglycans of the extracellular matrix are bound to proteins forming proteoglycans
questions.explanation: No official key — elastin provides elasticity; adhesion is via fibronectin/laminin.
